articles.title: For the Washington Spirit, will the third time be the charm in the NWSL championship?
articles.summary: The Washington Spirit hope the third time will be the charm as they face the Kansas City Current at home in the National Women’s Soccer League championship Saturday.
articles.body: The Washington Spirit hope the third time will be the charm as they face the Kansas City Current at home in the National Women’s Soccer League championship Saturday. Although the club won the title in 2021 and is considered to be among the most consistent in the league, the Spirit have fallen short in two consecutive years. They lost in 2024 against the Orlando Pride, who won their first championship after repeatedly failing to qualify for the playoffs, before falling in the final yet again to the last-seeded Gotham FC in 2025. This time, however, they’ll be able to claim home-field advantage. Every year, the NWSL chooses a neutral site to host the championship game ahead of the regular season. This year’s host just happens to be Audi Field, home of the Spirit and its MLS counterpart, D.C. United. The stadium is well known for the way the crowd’s roars reverberate, giving the field the nickname “Rowdy Audi.” “What we feel at Audi, I think, is something unique,” Spirit head coach Adrián González told reporters this week. “It’s a huge push of energy, a huge motivation, and sometimes with the game you have some adversities ... and that extra energy is a blessing, because we need them.” An inaugural NWSL team, the Spirit have made the league’s championship five times but have only reached the summit once, in 2021, star Trinity Rodman’s rookie season. Rodman, who recorded an assist on the game-winning goal that year, has become the face of the franchise with the backing of owner Michele Kang. But the team’s struggle to overcome late-season injuries has hampered the squad in the playoffs since. This year has been luckier, as they were able to activate veterans Ashley Hatch and Casey Krueger late in the season. Another addition has been Tanzanian forward Clara Luvanga, a former Al-Nassr player whose speed and hunger for goals has made her difficult to defend against. Luvanga scored once and had two assists in the Spirit’s quarterfinal win against the Portland Thorns, showcasing her relentless energy in front of the net, which wears down the opposition. This season has also been Rodman’s best to date. The 24-year-old recorded 12 goals in the regular season before adding another two on the score sheet against the Thorns. It’s a comeback story for Rodman, who spent much of 2025 recovering from a recurring back injury. But the Spirit aren’t the only team looking for redemption. Izzy Rodriguez, a defender for the Current, called it “surreal” to know the team will be back in the final. She said she’s ready to take in the moment and bring the competitiveness to the pitch. “Every playoff game has been a really tight game — that’s what you’re going to get in this league,” Rodriguez said Wednesday. “But I think we’re going to go out and be the best we can be.” The Current, an expansion team founded in 2021, made the final for the second time in franchise history. Kansas City had an incredible season last year, securing the postseason’s No. 1 spot at the fastest pace in NWSL history. But in a shocking upset, the Current were defeated by the last-seeded Gotham FC in the quarterfinals. It was a bitter end for the Current, who saw major roster turnover and injuries to key players early in the season. Expectation that the team would return to winning form at the start of the year, despite having forwards Temwa Chawinga and Michelle Cooper out with injuries, was unrealistic, according to head coach Chris Armas. This season came with a lot of change that led the team to discover a new version of itself, he added. “It just seemed like every time we steadied this ship, there was something there,” Armas said. “And on the inside, we just kept talking about staying steady, consistent, sticking to the process. ... I give the players a lot of credit, honestly.” In perhaps an ironic twist of fate, one of the saving graces for the Current this year has been the acquisition of former Spirit player Croix Bethune. The 25-year-old was drafted by Washington in 2024, winning Rookie of the Year in her first season even after missing the final two months with a torn meniscus suffered by throwing the ceremonial first pitch at a Nationals game. Her return the following year was lauded by both teammates and supporters as the young star seemed to rebound quickly early in the 2025 season. But Bethune was traded in February in a million-dollar transfer, with the Current paying the Spirit $900,000 in transfer funds and an additional $100,000 in allocation money. The deal was a preseason stunner as Bethune was a beloved fixture on the Spirit roster. To make matters worse for Spirit fans, this year has been Bethune’s best by far. The young midfielder had five goals and 11 assists and played nearly 2,200 minutes in the regular season. She was named the NWSL’s Midfielder of the Year on Wednesday night. Bethune will return to Audi on Saturday night to face her former team and fight for the biggest title of her career. The young star said she’s confident it will be an “amazing game” as both teams are on a roll in the postseason. “Going to Audi, it is tough for opponents to play against them because the stadium itself is great,” Bethune said Sunday after winning the semifinal game. “The fans show out for them. But K.C. does the same thing. ... I’m sure they’ll be there in D.C., too.”

articles.title: Liverpool fan found not guilty of racially abusing Antoine Semenyo
articles.summary: Mark Mogan was accused of shouting abuse at Antoine Semenyo at a match at Anfield in August 2025.
articles.body:
A Liverpool fan accused of racially abusing footballer Antoine Semenyo has been found not guilty after the player withdrew his support for the prosecution.

Semenyo was due to give evidence at Liverpool Magistrates' Court in the trial of Mark Mogan, 47, who was accused of shouting racist abuse during the opening match of the Premier League season at Anfield on 15 August last year.

But Simon Jones, prosecuting, said: "Following recent contact made with Mr Semenyo, he has indicated he is no longer supportive of proceedings and the prosecution do not consider it is appropriate to compel him.

"In those circumstances we offer no further evidence in the case."

District Judge Mary Dowrick recorded a verdict of not guilty to the charge of racially aggravated behaviour.

Semenyo, who was a Bournemouth player at the time of the incident but is now signed for Manchester City, had been due to give evidence last month but the trial was adjourned halfway through when Mogan was taken to hospital after suffering a seizure.

The court had heard that Mogan, in a wheelchair, shouted at Semenyo as he went to take a throw-in about 30 minutes into the game.

As he was preparing to take the throw-in Mogan allegedly shouted a racist insult.

Opening the case last month, Jones said: "That racial abuse was shouted directly at Antoine Semenyo, who was close to him.

"Mr Semenyo briefly froze, as he couldn't believe what the male had said."

Witnesses also said they saw him throw his chewing gum at the footballer.

Semenyo reported the incident to the match referee and Mogan was removed from the stadium at half-time.

Mogan, who had an intermediary with him in court, told police in an interview that Semenyo had called him a cripple after he shouted at the player to "hurry up".

Mogan, of Templehill Close in Dovecot, Liverpool, declined to comment as he left court.

articles.title: Nations League quarter-finals: England to face Norway in the last eight with a potential semi-final tie with Germany waiting
articles.summary: England have been drawn to face Norway in the UEFA Nations League quarter-finals; the quarter-finals will be two-leg ties and will take place in the March international break; Wales will face Slovenia and Republic of Ireland will take on Croatia in the A/B play-offs
articles.body:
Thomas Tuchel's side finished top of their group thanks to their dramatic 3-2 win over Spain at the Metropolitano Stadium, while Norway finished second behind Portugal in Group D.

The two sides met in the 2026 World Cup quarter-finals, with a Jude Bellingham goal in extra-time sending the Three Lions through to the last four.

Should England progress, they will meet Belgium or Germany in the semi-finals. The other two quarter-final ties have seen world champions Spain drawn with France and Netherlands take on Portugal.

The quarter-finals will be two-leg ties and will take place in the March international break, with the first legs between March 25-27 and the second legs between March 28-30.

This will then be followed by the Nations League Finals, which will be held between June 9 and June 13, 2027.

The tournament will feature two semi-finals, a third-place play-off and the final. The four semi-finalists will be invited to make bids to host the semi-finals and final.

Wales and Republic of Ireland discover play-off opponents

Wales and the Republic of Ireland have also learned who they will face in the Nations League A/B play-offs.

Wales avoided automatic relegation to League B after securing one of the two better last place finishers in League A, while Republic of Ireland finished runners-up in their League B group behind Austria.

Craig Bellamy's side will take on Slovenia, while Heimir Hallgrimsson's men will face Croatia.

The play-off ties will also take place during the March international break.

articles.title: Etxeberria, el relevo que más ha rendido en Segunda
articles.standfirst: Ningún técnico contratado con la Liga en marcha ha mejorado tanto a su equipo: el Alba ha pasado del 4,2 % de los puntos al 66,7 % con el de Elgoibar
articles.summary: Ningún técnico contratado con la Liga en marcha ha mejorado tanto a su equipo: el Alba ha pasado del 4,2 % de los puntos al 66,7 % con el de Elgoibar
articles.body: Siete equipos de Segunda han cambiado de entrenador con la Liga ya en marcha: Eldense, Albacete, Las Palmas, Leganés, Cádiz, Ceuta y Oviedo. Ninguno ha dado un salto como el del Alba. Etxeberria llegó tras la octava jornada cuando el equipo solo había sumado un empate y siete derrotas, es decir, con un punto de los 24 que disputó (4,2 %). El inicio del nuevo técnico no fue fácil: empezó perdiendo en Valladolid (5-0) y en Gijón (2-1), pero desde entonces ha ganado en Liga a Eldense, Sabadell, Leganés y Celta Fortuna. Cuatro seguidas. Suma 12 de 18 puntos, dos de cada tres en juego. Detrás aparece Javi Calleja. El Eldense había sumado 2 de 12 puntos con Claudio Barragán (16,7 %) y con él ha ganado 12 de los 27 que ha disputado (44,4 %). La mejora es clara, pero no llega a la mitad de la del Alba. Entre ambos estuvo el interino Josep Ferrando, que dirigió un solo partido y lo ganó en El Molinón (0-1). Lo de Las Palmas es distinto: Albert Sánchez tiene el mismo porcentaje que Etxeberria, un 66,7 %, pero en tres partidos, sumando 6 puntos de 9. Rubén de la Barrera había firmado 11 de 27 (40,7 %) y, entre medias, Juan Manuel Rodríguez sacó 3 de 6 en sus dos jornadas como interino. En Cádiz, Borja Jiménez lleva 4 de 12 (33,3 %). Albert Celades se había ido con 7 de 30 (23,3 %); él mismo había sustituido a Imanol Idiákez días antes del inicio de la Liga. En otros banquillos el cambio todavía no se nota. Luis Carrión lleva en el Leganés 4 puntos de 12 (33,3 %), algo menos que Rubén Albés, que dejó el equipo con 11 de 30 (36,7 %). Sergio Lobera y Raúl González solo han dirigido un partido, y los dos lo perdieron el pasado fin de semana: el Ceuta cayó 2-0 en Tenerife y el Oviedo, 1-2 ante el Girona. El cese de Julián Calero llamó la atención, porque se fue con 21 de 39 puntos (53,8 %) y justo después de ganar en Cádiz. José Juan Romero, en cambio, dejó al Ceuta colista, con 5 de 39 (12,8 %). De todos los recién llegados, solo Etxeberria ha ganado cuatro partidos seguidos en Liga. El domingo, en El Plantío, puede ir a por el quinto y de paso igualar el récord histórico del club en el fútbol profesional que firmó el Alba de Alberto González en la primavera de 2024. Etxeberria compareció este viernes en la previa del Burgos-Alba del domingo con una buena noticia: “Todavía queda alguna sesión, pero viendo un poco la evolución y que ya está entrenando con el grupo y a buen nivel, pues recuperamos a Munir”. El técnico aseguró que “casi a un 100 % va a venir convocado”. El regreso del hispanomarroquí llega con Higinio lesionado, aunque Etxeberria espera tenerlo de vuelta “en un par de semanas”. Lo de Víctor San Bartolomé está menos claro. Sufrió un fuerte esguince en Copa: “Se descartó cualquier lesión grave y veremos, todavía quedan un par de días, pero es duda”. Etxeberria no se engaña pese a las cuatro victorias seguidas en Liga: “Estamos en descenso y eso es duro; por mucho que llevemos una buena racha, queremos salir de ahí cuanto antes, ganar el domingo y salir de ahí”.

articles.title: England vs Jamaica netball series: Anna Stembridge says her side are facing one of strongest Jamaican teams in history
articles.summary: London's Copper Box will host the first two matches of the third Horizon Series between England and Jamaica, before the two sides face off in Kingston at the start of December
articles.body:
The Vitality Roses will play two matches against the Sunshine Girls at London's Copper Box this weekend before travelling to Kingston for a pair of away matches on December 5 and 6.

Jamaica shifted the traditional power dynamics in netball this year when they beat No 1-ranked Australia in the semi-finals of the Commonwealth Games, before losing to New Zealand in the final.

"We're hugely excited about playing them," said Stembridge.

"They've just come off taking the scalp against Australia and getting that silver medal. It's probably one of the best and most exciting Jamaica sides we've ever seen."

Saturday's fixture will be Stembridge's first since being appointed England's full-time head coach for the second time in her career.

She previously held the role between 2011-2015 and is relishing the opportunity of appearing in front of a home crowd.

"We love playing in London, we love playing at the Copper Box, the atmosphere is electric," she added.

"So super excited about playing at home.

"We have some brilliant role models in this group and a number of London-born and raised, so I'm hoping the London crowd are going to get right behind us."

England have selected a mix of experience and youth for this series, with 18-year-old Gracie Smith and 20-year-old Izzy Phillips coming into the squad alongside players such as Commonwealth Games winner Nat Metcalf.

"With Gracie and Izzy, I've been hugely impressed. The way they've just come about their work, they've got stuck into training, they're contributing beautifully in analysis sessions," Stembridge said.

"We're very excited, particularly about those two youngsters, but also when you look around the table, you look at Nat Metcalf who won gold in 2018.

"She's probably our most seasoned and experienced player. Having come back from having a daughter and that wealth of experience, you cannot underestimate it."

Cardwell vows to 'fight to the end for the Roses'

England's Eleanor Cardwell now has 81 international caps to her name, but her netball journey has been somewhat turbulent.

Throughout her career she has transitioned from goalkeeper to goal shooter and undergone two surgeries on her knee, which resulted in a 12-month absence from the court and the fear that she would never play again.

However, she is now eyeing a century of caps and insists the honour of representing her nation has not worn off.

"I've been on such a huge journey, going from 2016 to now," Cardwell said.

"I've had some ups and downs within those 10 years and I'd say, since my injury, I've had such a passion for getting back into this red dress and playing for this team again.

"Every time I get to sing that national anthem, it just feels like such a privilege to be there and I can't wait to fight until the end for the Roses.

"I would love to be in the century club, I'd love to be able to say that I've got 100 caps for England, but I will obviously do anything and everything it takes for my country."

Cardwell, affectionately nicknamed 'The Claw', highlighted Jamaica's athleticism and physicality as particular strong points, as well as the return of Jhaniele Fowler-Nembhard.

"Jhaniele is an incredible athlete, there's no denying that," she said.

"She was in the best form of her life before she had her little baby. You know that she's always just going to bring her A-game, but it's not only her.

"The Jamaican team has really gelled in the past two, three, four years and they've sorted out some, maybe, teething errors that they had."

Fowler-Nembhard building confidence ahead of World Cup

Fowler-Nembhard is widely considered the one of the greatest goal shooters to ever grace the court.

Her last appearance for the Sunshine Girls came at the Netball World Cup in 2023 and she then took an extended break from the game after the birth of her second child.

She now returns as co-captain alongside Shamera Sterling-Humphrey.

"I'm just grateful for being able to play netball and I'm humbled by the accolades," Fowler-Nembhard said.

The Jamaica star believes her side have "nothing to prove" coming into this weekend's series, but beating England would build confidence ahead of the 2027 World Cup in Australia.

"We know that it's always a good rivalry between us and England. If there's anything to prove, it's to ourselves to know that we have an even bigger tournament coming up next year," she said.

"It is going to be really crucial because beating any of the top three teams is going to be good for psychologically giving us a gauge as to where we are at. It's definitely going to set us up going into next year's World Cup.

"Making sure that we are also connecting as a team and knowing how the England players are and coming up against them and then how we look against them individually is going to be really good.

"I'm hoping that it inspires the next generation to want to be there as well and want to train hard, work hard to be in this position to also play for gold medals, to also defeat the likes of England, New Zealand and Australia."

articles.title: New MLS salary rankings: Messi takes nearly half of Inter Miami’s entire $59.37M payroll as four stars join him in league’s elite $10M club
articles.summary: Discover how Lionel Messi tops Major League Soccer's salary rankings with over $28 million, as four star players join him in the prestigious $10 million club. Learn about the significant rise in MLS player earnings and payroll statistics.
articles.body: Lionel Messi continues to lead Major League Soccer's salary rankings, with the Inter Miami forward earning more than $28 million in guaranteed compensation. The latest figures also show how the league's highest salaries are expanding, with Robert Lewandowski, Antoine Griezmann, Son Heung-Min and Breel Embolo joining Messi in the group earning more than $10 million. Across MLS, 150 players now receive at least $1 million in guaranteed compensation.Lionel Messi leads MLS salaries ahead of Robert Lewandowski and Antoine GriezmannMessi's guaranteed compensation stands at $28.33 million, unchanged from the previous spring salary release but significantly higher than the $20.45 million recorded a year earlier. The Argentine remains comfortably ahead of the rest of the league, with his Inter Miami contract making him MLS's highest-paid player.According to figures published by the MLS Players Association and reported by ESPN, four other players have joined Messi above the $10 million threshold. Chicago Fire forward Robert Lewandowski ranks second with guaranteed compensation of $19.51 million, followed by Orlando City striker Antoine Griezmann on $13.94 million.LAFC's Son Heung-Min earns $11.25 million, while Atlanta United forward Breel Embolo completes the five-player group with $10.81 million. The figures place five of MLS's biggest names in a salary bracket that previously had fewer representatives.All figures are as of October 9, 2026. Salaries for players who arrived during the summer transfer window have been annualised.Messi's guaranteed compensation does not represent his entire earnings from football and commercial arrangements. His wider income has been estimated at approximately $80 million annually, although that figure includes revenue beyond his MLS playing salary.Inter Miami lead MLS team spending as Philadelphia Union sit at the bottomInter Miami's investment in their squad is reflected in a league-high total payroll of $59.37 million. Chicago Fire rank second at $41.29 million, followed by Atlanta United, LA Galaxy and LAFC, each with payrolls exceeding $32 million.The gap between Miami and the rest of the league is considerable, with the club spending more than twice as much as 25 of the other 29 teams. Despite that outlay, Inter Miami finished second in the Eastern Conference during the regular season, behind Supporters' Shield winners Nashville SC, whose payroll was considerably lower at $24.97 million.At the other end of the spending table, Philadelphia Union had the league's lowest payroll at $12.64 million. Sporting Kansas City followed at $13.30 million, ahead of D.C. United ($14.55 million), CF Montreal ($15.02 million) and FC Dallas ($15.49 million).Philadelphia Union's 17-year-old phenom Cavan Sullivan earned $614,000 in guaranteed compensation, the highest ever for an MLS Homegrown player, yet still below the league average ($746,936) and roughly 2% of Lionel Messi's $28.33 million salary, highlighting the stark wage gap between domestic rising stars and imported global icons.MLS average salary rises 18 per cent as 150 players earn at least $1 millionThe increase in spending at the top of the salary table has accompanied broader growth across the league. Average guaranteed compensation for the MLS player pool reached $746,936, an 18 per cent rise from $632,809 in October 2025.The median guaranteed compensation increased by a more modest 6.4 per cent, reaching $360,042 from $338,347 over the same period. The distinction between the average and median figures reflects the influence of the league's highest earners, whose salaries pull the overall average considerably higher.A total of 150 players now earn at least $1 million in guaranteed compensation, although the average figure includes pool players and retired players who are still owed money. The latest figures therefore cover a wider group than just the active first-team players appearing regularly in MLS matches.The league and the MLS Players Association are currently in the sixth year of their collective bargaining agreement, signed in February 2021. The existing agreement runs until the end of 2027.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: England's Nations League 2027 route to the final: Norway quarter-final draw, potential Belgium or Germany semi-final and dates
articles.summary: Nations League 2026/27: England's route to the final explained, with Norway awaiting in the quarter-finals and Germany or Belgium possible semi-final opponents after the draw; world champions Spain will face France, while Netherlands take on holders Portugal in the last eight
articles.body:
Thomas Tuchel's side will face Norway in the quarter-finals , with a semi-final against either Belgium or Germany awaiting them should they progress.

The Three Lions secured top spot in their group with an impressive 3-2 victory over Spain in Madrid, earning themselves a seeded position for the knockout stages and the advantage of playing the second leg of their quarter-final at home.

England will travel to face Erling Haaland and Martin Odegaard's side in the first leg between March 25 and 27, before welcoming them to Wembley for the return fixture between March 28 and 30.

Norway secured their place in the last eight in dramatic fashion, coming from two goals behind to beat Denmark 3-2 and qualify at their opponents' expense.

Should England overcome that challenge, their route to the final would see them face the winner of Belgium vs Germany in the semi-finals.

Belgium finished runners-up in Group A1, while Germany topped Group A2 after inflicting a 5-0 defeat on Netherlands.

On the other side of the draw, world champions Spain will face France, while Netherlands take on holders Portugal. The winners of those two quarter-finals will meet in the other semi-final.

When are the Nations League quarter-finals?

The quarter-finals will be played over two legs during the March international break.

England will play away in Norway before hosting the return leg at Wembley.

When are the Nations League semi-finals and final?

The Nations League Finals will take place between June 9 and 13, 2027.

The four quarter-final winners will progress to the final tournament, which consists of two semi-finals, a third-place play-off and the final.

England will need to win their quarter-final and semi-final to reach the showpiece, where they will have the opportunity to be crowned champions of Europe in this competition.

The four semi-finalists will be invited to submit bids to host the final tournament.

articles.title: Ideal Transfers for Mauricio Pochettino and Manchester United in the 2027 Winter Window
articles.summary: Mauricio Pochettino's first transfer window at Manchester United simply needs to save the club from Premier League relegation.
articles.body:
Mauricio Pochettino's first transfer window at Manchester United simply needs to save the club from Premier League relegation.

The Red Devils are on a fast-track to the Championship with one win in their opening 10 matches. January's window needs to be about immediate improvement with players who are good enough to come in and do a job, while maintaining value for a long-term future at the club.

It's going to cost serious money to do such business mid-season.

Here's a selection of players Poch should look at as he takes his first sip from the most obvious poisoned chalice in sports...

Arguably Man United's most pressing need is an immediate replacement for Diogo Dalot. Someone who can come in and understand Poch's style without too much transition.

Hell, someone who can just do the basics without playing that Dalot-styled inside pass that keeps setting up chances for the opposition.

Poch's time with the USMNT ensures he will be linked to numerous American stars. Alex Freeman should be the most intriguing. The Villarreal full-back has the type of qualities United seem allergic to at the back; he's athletic, quick, and very good on the ball. He can also play on either side.

The 22-year-old is much-admired by Poch, who praised his humility, ability to listen and noted he can be "one of the best" players in the world if he continues the way he's going. That's legitimate admiration and shouldn't be taken lightly.

Now, an "ideal" transfer for Man United would be Newcastle's Lewis Hall. Just like it would have been in the summer, before he signed a new contract at St. James' Park. "Ideal" doesn't mean "likely".

He is the perfect profile of left-back for a Champions League-level club, although the Magpies' bad start to the campaign and his commitment has cooled reports that he might move on. At 22 years old he could have at least a decade of first-team football in him.

Hall's attacking instincts have contributed to Newcastle's best moments this season. Three assists and a goal across 18 matches are the kind of numbers Luke Shaw will struggle to hit by the end of May. Hall also plays with an aggression that constantly pushes the team forward, even if Newcastle have struggled to capitalise on it.

However, considering Man United's position, relatively poor finances and Poch's history, expect to see Fulham's Antonee Robinson mentioned a lot more instead.

It says a lot about Man United's current squad that so many potential signings are just players who have a strong, physical profile.

Poch's defensive options are bumbling. He'll quickly need to replenish the entire backline, but at least one centreback needs to come in during the winter window.

Everton's Jarrad Branthwaite is a player United have coveted for a long time, even placing a £50 million bid for him two years ago. Since then, the 24-year-old has had to deal with recurring injury issues, missing 31 games last season.

Although he's also sat out of five so far this campaign, he's been in excellent form across the nine Premier League appearances he has made.

Links to Fulham's Calvin Bassey are underwhelming. He's a good player, but United shouldn't be targeting players who could move to a mid-table Premier League side without people batting an eyelid. More ambition needs to be shown - and that means spending.

Bruno Fernandes' time at Old Trafford is coming to an end. Two contract rejections and record-breaking form has gone out the window for a player who just looks fed up to play for the club these days. That's fine - he deserves more than to scrap it out in a relegation dogfight.

That means Poch needs to identify an all-action midfielder who can create and contribute across the entire pitch.

One of his first signings at Tottenham was Dele Alli, a player whose tremendous quality lifted Spurs to the Champions League final before a fall from grace that now has him more prominently watched as a streamer than an active footballer. Poch got magic out of him, though.

Morgan Gibbs-White should be considered the ideal pick-up, although Nottingham Forest owner Evangelos Marinakis would likely make things very difficult, just like he did when Spurs were interested last year.

MGW isn't playing particularly well in a Forest side that have only scored nine goals in as many games, but he's still contributed to four of those with three assists and a goal for himself.

At 26 years old he should be involved in battles to qualify for the Champions League, not stay in the Premier League (not that Man United can help with that right now).

There was a time when Man United competed for the best young talent in the world. Imagine if Wayne Rooney was coming through as a 16-year-old right now. There's no chance in hell they'd get him.

That realisation should be a wake up call if the club ever wants to get back to acting like the elite entity that dominated for so long.

Winning the race for Eli Junior Kroupi would be considered a huge coup. The versatile Bournemouth forward continues to be linked with Arsenal, Barcelona and others. He likely would have moved in the summer for huge money if he didn't get injured.

The 13 goals he scored in his debut Premier League season is the most by any teenager in history, beating Robbie Fowler.

He has serious pedigree that even a completely stacked French national team recognises. The fact he can play anywhere across the frontline and No. 10 is going to make him an important addition for any side that eventually splashes the estimated £100 million fee to get him away from the Vitality Stadium.

Benjamin Sesko's injury issues have played a sizeable part in United's struggles this season.

Not having an alternative to Bryan Mbeumo means Michael Carrick entered most matches without an opportunity to mix things up or change the style of play. Although Joshua Zirkzee has performed well, he's heading towards the exit as soon as United land extra firepower.

Benfica's Vangelis Pavlidis should be on the club's radar. The Greek striker has remained prolific for years, scoring consistently across the Dutch league, Portuguese league, European competitions and on the international stage. His seven goals in the Champions League two seasons ago included a hat-trick against Barcelona.

Pavlidis is a great interlinker of play, a trait that would work well with Bruno, Mbeumo and Matheus Cunha buzzing around him. He'd allow each to get closer to goal, something Carrick struggled with in Sesko's absence. Most importantly, Pavlidis is just an excellent finisher who should be gettable.

United shouldn't settle for Folarin Balogun, who continues to be linked, just because of his association with Poch. They already have one striker who could play for Everton in Zirkzee. The ambition needs to be higher.

articles.title: Julián Alvarez apunta al Getafe
articles.standfirst: La Araña prolonga en su vuelta a los entrenamientos del Atlético la voracidad con la que marcó tres goles con Argentina durante el parón, postulándose para el once del Coliseum
articles.summary: La Araña prolonga en su vuelta a los entrenamientos del Atlético la voracidad con la que marcó tres goles con Argentina durante el parón, postulándose para el once del Coliseum
articles.body: Ocasión, gol; remate, a la jaula. Así volvió Julián Alvarez a los entrenamientos del Atlético, dando continuidad a la voracidad mostrada con Argentina durante un parón del que regresa con tres dianas en la mochila en apenas 135 minutos de juego. Un estado de gracia que directamente le catapulta al once que presentará Simeone el domingo en Getafe. No había vivido una dulce despedida la Araña después de fallar dos imperdonables mano a mano ante Joan García en la visita del Barcelona al Metropolitano, pero su estancia con la Albiceleste le ha permitido recuperar la sonrisa. Su gol a Uruguay y el doblete en la primera parte frente a Costa Rica han recargado su moral de nuevo. El mejor refuerzo anímico para volver a empezar e intentar lucir como en sus mejores días en un Atlético en el que sólo había celebrado dos tantos en lo que va de curso. De hecho, tras ese periplo goleador con su selección, su primera práctica como rojiblanco invita a pensar que ha recobrado la voracidad de su primera campaña. Al menos, atendiendo a sus ganas y, sobre todo, a su puntería. Así las cosas, Julián será la punta de lanza del equipo que Simeone viene ensayando en los últimos días, acompañado de Oblak, Llorente, Le Normand, Hancko, Grimaldo, Giuliano, Cardoso, Koke, Barrios y Baena. Al tiempo que Julián se salía de cara a puerta, el Cuti Romero continuaba con su proceso de rehabilitación en un campo anexo junto a uno de los recuperadores. En este sentido, tal y como adelantó MARCA el pasado martes, el argentino no estará disponible para Getafe al marchar su puesta a punto con más lentitud, y cautela, de lo previsto. Obviamente, tampoco entrará en la lista Lookman, mientras que Pubill también se antoja complicado por más que su esguince sea leve después de que este viernes haya trabajado en el gimnasio. Allí permaneció Hjulmand durante toda la sesión, si bien, en principio, por una cuestión de cargas tras disputar íntegros los 180 minutos de Dinamarca en este parón.

articles.title: Sonia Bermúdez: "Los minutos que restemos ahora multiplicarán en Brasil"
articles.standfirst: La seleccionadora puso en valor la cantera con la inclusión de hasta cinco novedades en la lista para los próximos amistosos
articles.summary: La seleccionadora puso en valor la cantera con la inclusión de hasta cinco novedades en la lista para los próximos amistosos
articles.body: Sonia Bermúdez compareció ante los medios de comunicación en el Salón Villalonga de la Ciudad del Fútbol de Las Rozas para valorar la convocatoria de los dos partidos amistosos que disputará España ante Chile y Venezuela los días 28 de noviembre y 4 de diciembre en León y A Coruña respectivamente. Una citación de 25 futbolistas tan destacada por la enjundia de las ausencias como por la meritocracia de las novedades. "Hay una competitividad muy alta. Traemos a jugadoras que están en buenos momentos. No es algo puntual, es algo que se han ganado en sus clubes. El abanico de jugadoras que vemos es muy amplio y valoramos su rendimiento", justificó la madrileña. La seleccionadora no quiso ahondar en la gestión de las bajas, pactadas en mucho caso, aunque apuntó al calendario y la carga de minutos como justificación. "Se ha priorizado gestionar la carga de minutos. Controlamos muchos las cargas y algunas son jugadoras que acarrean muchos minutos y molestias en algún caso", dijo. "También digo que las que entran se lo han ganado. Queremos verlas en contexto de absoluta y es un buen momento", destacó. "Los minutos que restemos ahora multiplicarán en Brasil", subrayó. "Hay dos partidos y veremos cómo gestionamos los minutos. Nunca ponemos en riesgo a ninguna futbolista. Hay un trabajo detrás sabiendo que podemos repartir muchos minutos", recalcó. Sobre los retornos, Sonia habló de Aitana Bonmatí y Olga Carmona, dos de las capitanas de la selección. "Aitana tiene todos los galones del mundo, es nuestra capitana. Es una futbolista fundamental que aún tiene que coger ritmo. Vamos a tener la paciencia para gestionar minutos y queremos tenerla en dinámica. Volver de una lesión tan larga y complicada no es fácil y lleva un proceso de recuperación, pero seguro que vamos a ver a una Aitana mejor de lo que era", expuso. "Olga empezó la temporada con una lesión en el isquio que arrastraba de antes, pero ahora está a un gran nivel. Es otra de nuestras capitanas y si viene es que está más que preparada", resolvió. Bermúdez puso en valor el trabajo y el valor de la cantera. "Es un ejemplo para todo el mundo. Otras selecciones nos preguntan por el trabajo que realizamos y quiero ponerlo en valor, tanto el de las categorías inferiores como el de las territoriales y los clubes. Creo que son jugadoras que nos pueden aportar mucho", afirmó. "Vamos a tener paciencia con estas jóvenes, aunque son jugadoras de mucho nivel y queremos verlas en contexto de la absoluta", destacó. A nivel individual, definió a Cecilia Marcos y Daniela Agote como "encaradoras" y dibujó a Silvia Cristóbal y Aïcha Camara como centrales. "Tenemos todas las posiciones bien cubiertas y jugadoras que pueden actuar en diferentes posiciones. Dependerá del rival, del contexto, del partido...", aseveró. España jugará ante Chile y Venezuela, dos rivales a los que nunca se ha enfrentado y que le propondrán cosas diferentes. "Son dos rivales que nos van a demandar cosas que queremos probar: bloque bajo, defensa de seis, transiciones, duelos... En cada convocatoria buscamos para prepararnos para contextos diferentes y que nos favorecen para estar listas para el Mundial", sentenció Sonia.

articles.title: Zabaleta, de las noches con Messi al gol del Kun que cambió la historia del City
articles.standfirst: El argentino repasa en La Pizarra de Quintana sus mejores anécdotas en el Espanyol, el Manchester City y la selección
articles.summary: El argentino repasa en La Pizarra de Quintana sus mejores anécdotas en el Espanyol, el Manchester City y la selección
articles.body: Pablo Zabaleta tenía 20 años cuando llegó a Barcelona y, entre sus primeros planes en la ciudad, estaba el de recoger a Leo Messi para ir a cenar. Años después, estuvo a punto de darle una Premier al Manchester City con su único gol de la temporada y jugó una final del Mundial con Argentina. El ex lateral pasó por La Pizarra de Quintana, en Radio MARCA, y puso una anécdota a cada etapa de su carrera. En una aparece la mirada del padre de Messi. En otra, el contrato que le habría pedido a Txiki Begiristain si el fútbol durase 45 minutos. Zabaleta y Messi llegaron al verano de 2005 como campeones del mundo sub-20. Uno acababa de fichar por el Espanyol y el otro empezaba a hacerse un sitio en el primer equipo del Barça. Solían cenar en Las Cuartetas, un restaurante argentino de Barcelona, y alguna noche seguían por la zona de Aribau. Como Messi todavía no tenía carné de conducir, Zabaleta lo recogía y lo llevaba de vuelta a casa. "El papá, con la mirada, me decía todo: 'Cuídame al nene'", recordó. El lateral bromeó con la responsabilidad que sentía cada vez que salían juntos. "Imagínate que pasa algo con Leo, estoy al horno". En el Espanyol también encontró a Mauricio Pochettino, que le ayudó a adaptarse y que ya daba indicaciones tácticas en los entrenamientos cuando todavía era futbolista. Y allí conoció a su mujer, aficionada perica como el resto de su familia. Cuando le preguntaron por un equipo en el que jamás habría jugado, se acordó de ella y de lo que había vivido durante sus tres temporadas de blanquiazul. "Se me hubiera hecho imposible haber jugado en el Barça". Si tiene que elegir su mejor recuerdo sobre el césped, Zabaleta se queda con la Premier de 2012. El Manchester City se jugaba el título en casa ante el Queens Park Rangers y se fue al descanso ganando 1-0 gracias a su único gol en aquella Liga. "Si esto termina así, imagínate, al día siguiente estoy tocando la puerta a Txiki Begiristain para pedirle cinco años más de contrato", bromeó. En el minuto 90, el City perdía 1-2 y necesitaba dos goles. Edin Džeko empató en el descuento y Zabaleta recordó un detalle de lo que pasó inmediatamente después. Según su relato, al QPR le avisaron desde el banquillo de que tenía la permanencia asegurada. En el saque de centro mandó el balón lejos y el City recuperó la posesión para lanzar el ataque que acabó con el gol de Sergio Agüero. "Yo creo que no tuve ni fuerza para ir a abrazarlo al Kun", contó. Después de pasar los últimos minutos convencido de que se les escapaba el título, recuerda que acabó en el suelo, vencido por la tensión. Begiristain también aparece en la historia del fichaje que estuvo más cerca de sacar a Zabaleta de Manchester. En 2016, con un año de contrato por delante y Guardiola a punto de llegar, el argentino tenía una oferta concreta de la Roma. Las conversaciones estaban avanzadas cuando el director deportivo del City le transmitió el mensaje que cambió sus planes. "Pep te quiere acá". Guardiola se sentó después con el lateral y le confirmó que contaba con él. Zabaleta se quedó y todavía agradece haber podido trabajar una temporada con el técnico. De sus años en el City también rescató el nombre de David Silva, uno de los compañeros con los que mejor se entendió. En los rondos, recordó, el canario "no estaba nunca en el medio". En los partidos, cuando Silva recibía entre líneas, a Zabaleta le bastaba con doblar por fuera. El pase llegaba a la medida para centrar. Entre los rivales que más le hicieron sufrir eligió a Ronaldinho y Eden Hazard. Para sacarle de quicio, se quedó con Diego Costa. Ya estaba amonestado en un partido ante el Chelsea cuando se enganchó con el delantero, protestó al árbitro y acabó expulsado. "Me gané la segunda amarilla", reconoció. Admite que conocía de sobra lo bien que provocaba Costa y que, aun así, cayó. El partido que Zabaleta pediría repetir es la final del Mundial de 2014 contra Alemania. Tenía 29 años y, nada más acabar, se preguntó si volvería a tener la oportunidad de jugar otra. Argentina había tenido ocasiones antes de encajar en la segunda parte de la prórroga. "Esa cicatriz de haber perdido difícilmente vaya a cerrar en mi vida", confesó. Ocho años después, ya retirado, vivió el título de Qatar mientras cubría el Mundial para un medio de comunicación. Se acordó de las dos finales de Copa América perdidas tras Brasil, de las críticas a Messi y de lo que también había sufrido Ángel Di María. Había compartido vestuario con los dos durante aquellos años y sabía lo que significaba para ellos volver a intentarlo. "Lloré como si lo hubiera ganado".

articles.body:
La firma de Xavi Espart, minuto a minuto

Muy buenas tardes. Xavi Espart firmará este viernes 20 de noviembre su nuevo contrato como culé hasta 2030. El joven defensa, ahora lesionado del tobillo, se ha convertido en una de las revelaciones en este arranque de temporada a las órdenes de Hansi Flick . articles.title: Reality Time for Wake Forest
articles.summary: Call it a “trap game.” Call it the next step to a conference championship opportunity. What it is is reality time for Wake Forest. The Demon Deacons travel t...
articles.body:
Call it a "trap game." Call it the next step to a conference championship opportunity. What it is is reality time for Wake Forest. The Demon Deacons travel to Atlanta to face Georgia Tech Saturday afternoon, with everything they have accomplished thus far on the line.

Wake is the newly anointed number 11 team in the College Football Playoff rankings with a 9-1 overall record. That #11 spot makes them the last at-large team that would make the playoff this year. The #12 slot will go to a Group of Six school since none of them are ranked in the top 12 on their own. One slip over the last two weeks of the regular season and the blow to Wake's season will be felt for years to come.

Even though Georgia Tech is in last place in the ACC with a 3-7 overall record and a 2-5 conference record, Wake head coach Jake Dickert is working to make sure no one takes the Yellowjackets for granted. They did, after all, just beat Clemson on the road last week by two touchdowns. "I've said this, and I really believe it. I think they are the most talented 3-7 team in the country," Dickert said earlier this week.

Of course, the two schools do not play every year, but Wake has lost the last five matchups between the two. The last time Wake beat GA Tech was 2006, 9-6.

Last year's game in Winston-Salem still leaves a bad taste in the mouth of most Wake fans. After Wake running back Demond Claiborne scored on a 25-yard run to make it a 30-29 GA Tech lead in the second overtime, the Deacs went for two. Claiborne was hobbled. Quarterback Robby Ashford was hobbled. His pass into the end zone for the two points was intercepted, and the Deacs lost by one. Of course, there was also the missed offside call against GA Tech late in the game that shut down a Wake Forest drive.

But Dickert and the Deacs have moved on from that, even if the fans never did. "This team, this moment, this timeframe, our energy and focus needs to be right here and right now."

He did have one piece of advice for the team this week that goes back to last year's game. "Don't leave it in anyone else's hands. Go out and win the game. No excuses. Nothing else matters but what happens at the end of the day on the scoreboard."

This is obviously a different GA Tech in 2026 as it is. Quarterback Haynes King and his dual-threat abilities are gone. Alberto Mendoza , the younger brother of 2025 Heisman winner Fernando Mendoza is the starting quarterback. The transfer from Indiana threw for 138 yards in the win over Clemson last week. He has 11 touchdown passes and seven interceptions on the season.

But Georgia Tech head coach Brent Key used two quarterbacks, with Gary Adamson also playing. He is not a threat in the passing game, but he ran 19 times for 87 yards and a touchdown. Key said this week that he intends to use both quarterbacks again against Wake Forest. Dickert said he thinks that scheme caught Clemson unprepared because it was not something GA Tech had utilized much this season.

Needless to say, Dickert and his staff have taken in as much of last week's Clemson game as one could in a few days.

Key knows points and ball control are going to be key for his squad against a Wake Forest team that has not lost a game in nearly two months. Asked this week what impressed him about Wake Forest, Key said, "All three phases of the game." He had particular praise for Deacs' quarterback Gio Lopez. "Gio is a tremendous college quarterback," he said. "You can tell the guys around him play to his level. He elevates the people around him."

At his weekly press conference on Monday, Dickert called the 49-7 win over SMU the best game of the season in terms of his team's performance. "After watching the SMU tape, the biggest thing I emphasized this morning (Monday) was this was a complete team win." He gave particular praise to the defense. "Our defense was just phenomenal. That's two years in a row of just stopping, really completely stopping a really good offense." He said, "I really believe it was our best team performance."

After weeks of saying he would not have time or care to watch the weekly unveiling of the College Football Playoff rankings , Dickert admitted on Wednesday that he did watch Tuesday night's show. He couched it as watching whatever came on after the Illinois-Duke basketball game.

"I think at the end of the day, I'm probably not going to change my tune," he said. "None of it matters if we don't take care of business this week. If we keep playing our way, we have a clear path. We've got to keep staying to the standard of which we play."

articles.title: “Fire Him Tonight,” “Make Him Walk Back to Indy”: Colts Fans Call for Shane Steichen’s Exit After Humiliating 26–3 Loss to Texans
articles.summary: Indianapolis Colts head coach Shane Steichen’s job security may be in question after the humiliating 26-3 defeat to the Houston Texans on Thursday Night Foot...
articles.body:
Indianapolis Colts head coach Shane Steichen's job security may be in question after the humiliating 26-3 defeat to the Houston Texans on Thursday Night Football. The loss dropped Indianapolis to 3-8, while Houston improved to 4-6. With general manager Chris Ballard already dismissed, Steichen could face similar scrutiny over the miserable Colts season.

In the blowout loss, Steichen's decision to attempt long field goals didn't pay off. A 56-yard attempt was missed, while a 62-yard attempt was blocked. Houston built a 17-3 halftime lead and never relinquished control.

"Colts need to fire him [Shane Steichen] tonight; complete dogwater game management," one fan commented.

"FIRE NOW and make him walk back to Indy," one fan wrote.

"Leave Shane Steichen in Houston," one fan said.

"FIRE SHANE STEICHEN ALREADY!" one fan commented.

"Shane Steichen shouldn't survive the mini bye," one fan remarked.

"Like right now. That was a national embarrassment," one fan wrote.

In the defeat against the Texans, the Colts offense struggled to generate momentum, finishing with only 167 total yards. Colts quarterback Daniel Jones went 12-of-27 for 144 yards and one interception.

On the other hand, Texans quarterback CJ Stroud threw three touchdown passes against one interception while completing 21 of 27 passes.

Shane Steichen's Contract In Focus After Colts Dropped to 3-8

Despite falling to 3-8 this season, Colts head coach Shane Steichen still has two seasons remaining on his contract. In Feb. 2023, he signed a six-year deal. If the Colts decide to fire Steichen before the season ends, they will have to pay for the remaining part of his contract.

On Oct. 19, when the Colts fired general manager Chris Ballard, Steichen survived the major shake-up as the front office has also traded away veteran players before the trade deadline.

Previously, following the Colts' defeat against the Jacksonville Jaguars, Steichen was asked about his future.

"I'm focused on getting better," Steichen said . "That's what I'm focused on right now."

"We have a lot to fix," Steichen added. "I've been saying that for a while. I understand that in this league, it's fricking hard; you've got to find ways to win games. You've got to find ways to get out of holes. Right now, we're not doing that good enough."

It's unclear if Indianapolis is thinking about firing Steichen. After taking over the Colts in 2023, Steichen has led Indianapolis to a 28-34 record and has not led them into the playoffs so far.

articles.title: Anselmi: “Me enamora lo que hacemos”
articles.standfirst: El entrenador del Elche siente que su equipo va “bien encaminado” para lograr la salvación y no espera a un Levante “encerrado”
articles.summary: El entrenador del Elche siente que su equipo va “bien encaminado” para lograr la salvación y no espera a un Levante “encerrado”
articles.body: El entrenador del Elche, Martín Anselmi, ofreció la rueda de prensa a la visita de su equipo al Levante (lunes, 21:00 horas, Ciutat de València), en un duelo directo por la salvación. Duelo directo por la salvación: “Desde que terminó el partido contra el Betis (0-2), más allá del necesario descanso, mi deseo es volver a jugar. Más allá del rival que tengamos enfrente. Veo al equipo que juega y compite bien, más allá del rival y de si jugamos local o visitante. Ese deseo lo tienen también los jugadores. Con ese ruido de la estadística, nuestro deseo es volver a competir. Nos quedamos con esa espina del último partido. Nos llevamos poco y queremos más. Toca un rival que está en una situación similar, así que mejor todavía”. Altas y bajas: “Lemar está con el grupo de manera total. Sabemos lo de Marc (Aguado), Yago y Adam (bajas). Es ir viendo día a día cómo se sienten los jugadores. Si un jugador completa entrenamientos antes del partido es porque puede estar de inicio”. ¿Casi una final?: “Competimos siempre para ganar. Nuestro deber es competir al máximo para ello. Si lo hacemos, estaremos cumpliendo con nuestro trabajo. Tengo mucho deseo de llevarme los tres puntos, más allá de la tabla o el rival. Vamos con la obligación de competir como lo estamos haciendo”. ¿Qué partido esperas?: “No creo que especulen tanto, juegan en casa. Irán a buscar el resultado. Espero un Levante que busque atacarnos. Lucha hasta el final y sabe lo que hace. Contragolpear rápido es la tónica del Levante, con transiciones rápidas. Pero no espero un rival encerrado”. ¿El equipo merece estar en descenso?: “Me cuesta la palabra ‘merecer’ en el fútbol. El proceso te lleva al objetivo. El equipo está haciendo un buen proceso. Si uno de los objetivos es acabar la temporada fuera del descenso, vamos bien encaminados a ello. Estamos más cerca de cumplir el objetivo que de no hacerlo”. Trabajo durante el parón: “Reforzamos lo que venimos haciendo. Hay detalles que provocan que estemos teniendo menos situaciones de gol de las que podríamos tener. Estamos trabajando bien. También era un momento de descansar, porque acumulamos muchísimas sesiones”. Posibles cambios en el once: “Hay muchos análisis para elegir un once. Historial de partido, entrenamientos...a partir de esas variables e información, elegimos. Estamos todavía lejos del partido, quedan dos entrenamientos. Pero ni las derrotas nos acercan a muchos cambios. Ni las victorias a la continuidad. Esto va de rendimientos. Lo importante es que todos estén a la altura competitiva”. Buonanotte: “Le veo bien. Hay más análisis dentro de las situaciones y contextos de cada futbolista. Falta de confianza, no te ayuda el contexto...cada jugador es un mundo. Me tengo que basar en lo que veo cada día. Veo deseo de ser mejores. Después, cada partido es un capítulo diferente. Y una oportunidad de mejorar. Los jugadores tienen picos. Cuando eres joven y demostraste mucho, no es fácil. Me ha pasado con jugadores que surgen, los compran, vuelan alto y luego tienen picos...hasta que encuentran el equilibrio. Facu está reencontrándose con ese futbolista que supo ser. Sabe que lo tiene dentro. El proceso no es ciencia, son seres humanos. Le veo bien y con ganas”. Lomónaco, sin debutar en Liga: “¿No se preguntan por qué no juega el suplente de Cubarsí? Tenemos razonamientos muy lineales. No soy quién para decirles cómo deben hacer su trabajo. Uno: lo que costó o no costó un jugador es irrelevante. Es del club, como cualquier otro. Dos: que juegue o no juegue no tiene nada que ver sólo con el físico o lo que costó. Entendemos que los que están jugando están bien. Lomónaco jugó en Copa. Si no ha jugado en Liga es porque los partidos no lo pidieron. Y porque los que están lo están haciendo bien. Lomónaco entiende lo que tiene que hacer, lleva tres meses aquí. Es muy positivo para el grupo. Va siendo mejor. Puede jugar, como otros. Pero vemos que estamos defendiendo bien con los que juegan. Cuando le toque jugar, lo hará bien. No llegó en la mejor condición física, pero ahora sí lo está. Que juegue dependerá de muchas circunstancias. Pero está preparado”. ¿Satisfecho con el trabajo?: “Esta semana, pensé/sentí esto: los entrenadores no nos enamoramos de todos los procesos en los que trabajamos. Debe haber excepciones. Cada proceso tiene su aprendizaje, con sus buenos y malos momentos. Esta semana, pensaba que me enamora lo que estamos haciendo. Lo sentí en el último partido. Somos valientes, competimos. Nadie nos supera con facilidad. Me enamora lo que hacemos, y eso no me pasaba en los anteriores procesos de mi carrera. Estoy feliz en el lugar. No sólo por el club, también la ciudad, el staff, la afición...y por cómo lo hacen los jugadores en el campo”.

articles.title: 'We Know How It Works': Head Coach Makes Transfer Claim Amid Chelsea Midfielder Interest
articles.summary: Marco Rose clarified his stance on Alex Scott's future at Bournemouth amid interest from other clubs, including Chelsea.
articles.body:
Bournemouth head coach Marco Rose has had his say on reported transfer interest, including from Chelsea, in star midfielder Alex Scott.

The January transfer window is inching closer, and many clubs are preparing for potential mid-season player acquisitions and sales.

For Chelsea , a new midfielder is likely high on their transfer wish list, after failing to secure a replacement for Enzo Fernandez, who joined Manchester City late in the summer.

According to Sky Sports , Chelsea "remain persistent" in their interest in Bournemouth midfielder Scott, who will soon enter the final 18 months of his contract with the Cherries.

The transfer race for the England international has intensified, with Arsenal understood to have entered the race alongside Chelsea and Liverpool . However, Chelsea remain in a strong financial position to close the deal if they can convince Bournemouth to sell their star player.

Bournemouth owner Bill Foley has recently made it clear that they have not given up on contract negotiations with Scott . But as long as the 23-year-old does not agree to a new deal, Bournemouth will understandably be under pressure to cash in on the player.

Interestingly, speaking at Thursday's press conference, Bournemouth boss Rose insisted he has not personally pushed Scott to pen a new deal.

"I don't need to do these kinds of things," Rose responded when asked whether he felt the need to convince Scott to extend his contract amid transfer interest from top Premier League clubs.

"We talk every day about football, about personal stuff. I think we have a good connection, and we know how it works in this business.

"Bournemouth are a top club for young players to improve, and he's, as we've always said, quite committed to the club. The rumours around (him), we can't change (it).

"He's a player of AFC Bournemouth, and he likes to be a player of AFC Bournemouth. The other things are of no interest to me as a coach."

Scott is reportedly not the only name on Chelsea's midfield shortlist. It is worth noting that Chelsea also made approaches for Roma's Manu Kone and AS Monaco's Lamine Camara late in the summer window.

The Blues were very close to signing the latter, before the deal collapsed after Monaco made a surprise U-turn on the agreement .

However, it is easy to see why they did not abandon their pursuit of Scott despite having their £64 million offer turned down by Bournemouth in the summer.

He is a very versatile centre midfielder, capable of playing in deeper and more advanced midfield roles. He excels in transitioning the ball from defence to attack, either by passing or carrying the ball himself, and is a reliable defender in the middle of the pitch.

The possible bidding wars for him in January or in the summer are far from ideal from Chelsea's perspective, but it is normal for a highly coveted young talent. As it stands, Chelsea have Moises Caicedo, Romeo Lavia, Jordan Henderson, and Valentin Barco as central midfield options. Two right-backs, Reece James and Malo Gusto, are also capable of playing in midfield.

articles.title: Andriy Shevchenko slams Mykhailo Mudryk for ‘baseless slander’ after Ukraine doping claim
articles.summary: Shevchenko, who is president of the Ukrainian football federation, called on Mudryk to provide evidence for his claims or retract his accusations
articles.body:
Ukrainian football federation president Andriy Shevchenko has issued a sharp rebuke to Mykhailo Mudryk after the Chelsea winger blamed the national team for his positive drugs test.

Mudryk tested positive for the banned substance meldonium in 2024 , and was initially banned for four years by the Football Association . He successfully appealed against the length of his ban to the Court of Arbitration for Sport , and returned to football in July 2026.

Speaking in an interview with Ukrainian YouTube channel Guest of Gordon, Mudryk, who is on a season-long loan at Tottenham, laid the blame on "the environment in the Ukrainian national team" for his suspension.

He said: "I had never heard of a drug like meldonium . It is a drug you can only get in Eastern Europe. It could only have got into my body in Ukraine. There is no such drug in England."

He said he had only been in Ukraine with the national team, which "points to the fact it was in a national team camp".

Former Chelsea and AC Milan forward Shevchenko, now president of the Ukrainian Association of Football (UAF), called such claims "baseless slander" and said that "numerous investigations and audits" had been unable to identify how or when the meldonium entered Mudryk's system.

He alleged that Mudryk's camp had tried to convince a staff member at the UAF to take the blame for the 25-year-old's positive test.

Shevchenko said: "His representatives repeatedly approached the UAF with a proposal to find an employee who would falsely take responsibility for the meldonium found in his doping sample.

"The UAF refused, as such a proposal contradicts the principles of our work."

Shevchenko criticised his compatriot for "baseless slander against our people, who do their work honestly and professionally", and challenged Mudryk to provide evidence for his claims, including that he had received little support from the federation during the doping case.

He added: "I know the people who have worked with the national team for many years. I trust them, because throughout all this time there have been no incidents in the team that could make anyone doubt their professionalism.

"If Mykhailo has evidence to back up his words, let him provide it. If no such evidence exists, I expect him to publicly retract his accusations and apologise to the people whose honesty and professionalism he has called into question."

With the international break out of the way, Real Madrid are back in action on Sunday as they get set to lock horns with Celta Vigo at the Santiago Bernabeu on Matchday 13 of the 2026/27 La Liga.

Having strung together an impressive run of eight wins prior to the break, Real Madrid will be eager to carry on from where they left off and secure all three points against Claudio Giraldez & co. tomorrow.

Ahead of tomorrow's match, Los Blancos manager Jose Mourinho has announced the squad list of players who will be at his disposal for selection.

The biggest headline is that key superstar Vinicius Jr. is back in the squad for Real Madrid after having missed the last four games in La Liga due to a suspension for his red card against Villarreal.

The 26-year-old attacker has missed the games against Sevilla, Barcelona, Racing Santander, and Valencia. Having scored five goals in two games for Brazil during the international break, he will hope to carry on in the same vein of form for his club.

Aurelien Tchouameni and Bernardo Silva, who returned with minor injuries during the break, have been declared fit and are in the squad to face Celta Vigo.

Meanwhile, Raul Asencio and Rodrygo remain unavailable as they continue to recover from their fitness issues.

Ferland Mendy was expected to be recalled to the squad, having been training with the group for some time now, but Mourinho has opted not to include the veteran left-back.

articles.title: Maddy Cusack: Inquest into death of Sheffield United Women midfielder to resume in December
articles.summary: Maddy Cusack died in September 2023 while a player at Sheffield United; an inquest began earlier this year, but was postponed in July to gather more evidence from the club; the inquest has previously been postponed, having initially been set to start in January 2026
articles.body:
Cusack's family sent a written complaint to United within a week after she died, outlining issues they alleged stemmed from her time working under her coach Jonathan Morgan.

The 27-year-old was found unresponsive at her home in Horsley, Derbyshire, on September 20 2023, after Morgan made comments about her weight and relationship with another player, Chesterfield Coroner's Court heard.

Assistant coroner Sophie Cartwright KC heard eight days of evidence from Morgan, Cusack's parents, her former team-mates, and members of staff from United, before the inquest was adjourned in July to get more evidence from the club.

United was asked by the coroner to look at its Microsoft Teams folders and Google Drive records for any information related to Cusack, and complete an audit of her health records on the club's system in the months before she died.

Cartwright told a pre-inquest hearing on Friday: "The inquest remains listed to recommence on the seventh of December, with a five-day listing."

The court heard the final evidence will be heard in Derby, where 11 witnesses are expected to be called.

The inquest was meant to begin in January but was postponed just before Christmas last year because of delays in disclosure of information to Cusack's family.

The coroner asked the player's relatives on Friday to provide any more text messages that may be relevant to the inquest, acknowledging the "emotional upset" they might experience by accessing her phone again.

Cusack's mother Deborah Cusack is expected to give more evidence next month, after she said Morgan was her daughter's "nemesis" who was referred to as a "prison warden" in messages between team-mates.

Deborah Cusack told the former United coach earlier this year: "There's a direct line - if you hadn't been employed, Maddy would be here today."

The inquest has previously heard that Morgan called Maddy Cusack "bottom heavy", which he said was referencing her muscular legs, and said "here come the girlfriends" when she was walking with her partner and United team-mate Grace Riglar.

He denied calling Cusack a "psycho" from the sidelines during a match before he joined United.

Asked about a comment he made calling her "generally a liar" in an account to the Football Association, Morgan had said she "omitted information" to her family about how he had supported her.

articles.title: Álvaro Núñez y Jones El-Abdellaoui reciben el alta y viajan a Madrid
articles.standfirst: Miguel Román, Borja Iglesias y Starfelt siguen de baja
articles.summary: Miguel Román, Borja Iglesias y Starfelt siguen de baja
articles.body: Álvaro Núñez y Jones El-Abdellaoui recibieron este viernes el alta médica y con ello el Celta comienza a despejar su enfermería, bastante repleta de futbolistas durante el primer tercio de campeonato. Ambos futbolistas entran en la convocatoria de 24 jugadores para el partido de este sábado en el Bernabéu. El atacante llevaba dos meses de baja por un pequeño cuerpo libre en la rodilla derecha que le obligó a un tratamiento quirúrgico mediante artroscopia. El marroquí esta temporada apenas pudo disputar 3 encuentros de Liga sumando 153 minutos. Mientras, Álvaro Núñez recibe el alta un mes después de sufrir una rotura fibrilar en el aductor de la pierna izquierda. Al defensa le llegó la lesión cuando atravesada por su mejor momento desde que llegase al club vigués. Hasta caer lesionado, había disputado 6 encuentros y un total de 437 minutos. A pesar de recuperar a estos dos futbolistas, Claudio Giráldez sigue sin poder contar con Borja Iglesias, Carl Starfelt y Miguel Román. Ninguno de ellos todavía trabaja con el grupo y entrenan de forma individual y, evidentemente, son bajas para el encuentro ante el Real Madrid.

articles.title: Nations League quarterfinal draw: Spain face France, England play Norway
articles.summary: World Cup winners and European champions Spain have reached three of the four Nations League finals, winning in 2023.
articles.body:
World champions Spain will face France while England will play Norway in the quarterfinals of the UEFA Nations League after the draw took place on Friday.

Spain beat France 2-0 in the semifinals of the World Cup in the United States in July on the way to winning the trophy . They also defeated Les Bleus 5-4 in the semifinals of the last edition of the Nations League last year.

The quarterfinals will be played over two legs in late March with Spain at home first after coming second in Group A3 while France topped Group A1 .

Spain won the Nations League in 2023 while France beat them to win the 2021 final.

England topped Group A3 on goal difference after beating Spain away in their last outing, and their reward is a two-legged last-eight tie with Norway with the first leg on Norwegian soil.

England edged Norway in the World Cup quarterfinals this year before losing to Argentina in the semifinals.

The other quarterfinal ties will pit reigning Nations League champions Portugal against the Netherlands and Belgium against Germany.

The winners of the quarterfinals will advance to the final stages, which will be held in June at a venue yet to be decided.

Spain or France will play the Netherlands or Portugal in the single-leg semis, and England would face Belgium or Germany should they get past Norway.

articles.title: Man City vs Fulham: Match Preview, Latest Team News and Score Prediction
articles.summary: Man City vs Fulham Preview: Pressure Builds on Enzo Maresca as Cottagers Eye Etihad UpsetManchester City have gone from setting the pace to chasing it. Seven...
articles.body:
Man City vs Fulham Preview: Pressure Builds on Enzo Maresca as Cottagers Eye Etihad Upset

Manchester City have gone from setting the pace to chasing it. Seven straight Premier League wins opened the campaign, then reality hit. Three consecutive defeats have dragged Enzo Maresca's side down to third, six points behind Arsenal. Form changes quickly in this league, but the numbers now matter and City's trend is ugly.

Normally, Fulham would be the ideal opponent to stop the slide. City have beaten the Cottagers in their last 17 top-flight meetings. Stretch that across all competitions and it becomes 20 in a row. That is not a rivalry, it is a pattern. The problem for City is that patterns only last until they don't.

Fulham arrive in better shape than many will expect. Alvaro Arbeloa's side have taken eight points from their last four league matches, built on two wins and two draws. While City have taken nothing from their last three, Fulham have been organised, stubborn and increasingly awkward to play against. Those are useful traits when heading to the Etihad.

The losses to Aston Villa, Brighton and Nottingham Forest were not a blip because there have now been three of them, and all exposed something. City were beaten 2-1 by Villa, edged out 1-0 by Brighton and then conceded three in a 3-1 defeat at Forest. That sequence tells its own story. They are not controlling matches well enough and they are giving opponents too many openings.

Selection issues in defence only add to the concern. Marc Guehi is a major doubt after asking to come off at half-time against Nottingham Forest and then withdrawing from England duty. Abdukodir Khusanov also needs assessing after leaving Uzbekistan's squad. If neither makes it, Josko Gvardiol may have to move inside from left-back, with Nico O'Reilly potentially returning to the side.

Antoine Semenyo remains unavailable with a knee injury and is not expected back until December. None of this amounts to a crisis on its own, but when a team is already losing games, defensive uncertainty tends to get magnified.

Fulham form offers genuine encouragement

Fulham's case is straightforward. They are compact, harder to break down and carrying enough belief to think they can frustrate City for long periods. Josh King went off late in the 1-1 draw with Newcastle, though Arbeloa said it looked like "nothing serious", and the player himself stated he was "all good fitness-wise". That points towards availability.

Tom Cairney is less certain after his knee issue, while Joachim Andersen appears likely to be involved despite picking up a foot injury on international duty and then completing 90 minutes in Denmark's next match. Up front, Rodrigo Muniz has given Arbeloa a decision to make after scoring from the bench against Newcastle, with Gonzalo Garcia under pressure for his starting place.

More importantly, Fulham's recent away work deserves attention. They drew 0-0 at Liverpool and fully earned it. They also took a 1-1 result at Villa Park. Those are not smash-and-grab outcomes, they are signs of a side that knows how to stay in games away from home.

This comes down to trust. Right now, City have not earned much of it. Fulham have. That does not mean Fulham are suddenly favourites, because City still have the better squad and the stronger attacking ceiling. It does mean the game should be viewed through form, not through old results.

If City start sharply, the crowd settles and the narrative changes. If Fulham keep it tight for an hour, anxiety will creep in. That is where this becomes interesting.

The sensible call is a low-scoring match and a very live chance of dropped points for the home side. Fulham have shown at difficult grounds that they can stay compact and disciplined, and City have shown over the last three games that they can be rattled.
